dedupe_keys.name: india district panel of rural electrification electrified wells and groundwater irrigation over three decades ray and pullabhotla 2023

description: This dataset is a panel of Indian districts spanning three decades that links rural household electrification, electrified groundwater wells and irrigated cropland, built to measure how electricity supply for pumping drives agricultural growth. The authors use it to show that after the government shifted its focus to universal household electrification in the early 2000s, districts electrified later gained about two electrified wells per 100 newly electrified households, against 16 in districts electrified earlier, and would have had nearly 20% more dry-season irrigated cropland without the shift. It was assembled by Sudatta Ray and Hemant K. Pullabhotla and published with an article in Nature Communications on 25 October 2023. Coverage is district level across India. The article is free under CC BY 4.0, and all replication data and code are available to download from a public repository linked in the article. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): CC-BY-4.0 (Zenodo record). For simulation it quantifies the dependence of irrigated agriculture on the rural power supply, useful for energy and water interdependency models and for scenarios of feeder rationing or outages. It is related to the global groundwater irrigation inventory record in this catalogue. The underlying files were not downloaded, so their contents are not verified here.
